svg.title: Indeed each occurrence first receives δiWj, the allocation among at most H occurrences gives the factor δi/H, and moving its support to the chosen representative costs exp((ei + 1 2)l). The occurrence sets of distinct groups partition the old occurrences, so Q γ W ′ γ = λi(H, l)s Q j Wj exactly. This proves the group-product formula used in (OE8). To obtain the grouped local functions, apply the finite marker fusion estimate to those oc- currence sets, using the cover bound l, the occupancy bound, and the two smallness inequalities
